body:
Today, Paul's words in Galatians stayed with me:

“For freedom Christ set us free.” At first, I struggled to understand what he meant. If Christ has set us free, why do we sometimes feel so burdened?

I know that I love God. Yet I also know how easily restlessness enters my heart. Worries about tomorrow, disappointments from yesterday, and responsibilities that seem never to end can leave little room for joy. Sometimes I become disappointed in myself because I cannot simply rest in God's love.

But perhaps I have been expecting freedom to mean the absence of struggle.

Paul was teaching that our relationship with God is founded upon His grace, not something we can earn through our own efforts. Christ did not come to make us carry another burden of proving ourselves worthy.

And I wonder how often we turn even our spiritual lives into another responsibility. We try harder to be patient, more loving, more trusting, more joyful. When the same difficulties return, we believe we must begin again.

But perhaps we are not beginning again. Perhaps we are continuing to grow.

Recently, while attending Mass, I watched people walking forward to receive the Body of Christ. One after another, they approached Him. I felt such unexpected joy, simply witnessing so many people choosing Christ.

For those moments, I wasn't thinking about my own shortcomings or what tomorrow might bring. I was simply happy to see others coming to Him.

It reminded me that love and joy are not absent simply because life is difficult.

Today's Gospel tells of people asking Jesus for another sign, even though He was already among them. I wonder how often I overlook what God has already placed before me because my attention is consumed by what remains unresolved.

Perhaps freedom does not mean every burden disappears. Perhaps it means that while we carry what life requires of us, we need not measure God's love by how well we are managing it.

There are responsibilities we must attend to, losses we must acknowledge, and problems that still need answers. Faith does not erase them. But neither must they become the measure of our lives.

I am learning that I do not have to feel peaceful every moment to belong to Christ. I do not have to manufacture joy or condemn myself when worry returns.

Sometimes I can simply look toward Him, remember the love I witnessed in those approaching the Eucharist, and recognize that His grace is still at work.

Maybe that is where freedom begins: not when life finally becomes easier, but when we stop believing we must resolve everything before allowing ourselves to be loved.
prayer: Lord Jesus,  You know the burdens I carry and the worries that return even when I try to surrender them.  Forgive me when I measure my faith by how peaceful I feel. Teach me to recognize Your grace in ordinary moments and to welcome the joy You place before me.  Give me strength for what I must do, wisdom to know what I cannot control, and a heart willing to rest in Your love.  Amen.
scripture: Galatians 4:22–24, 26–27, 31—5:1 Gospel: Luke 11:29–32 Additional Scripture: Galatians 5:22–23; John 15:11
title: In Christ there is Freedom
theme: Can we find joy in God's love even when life's burdens remain?
opening: What if the very thing we have been searching for is something we have already been given? We spend so much of our lives trying to find peace, yet sometimes the harder we try, the further away it seems. Could we be overlooking something?
